record.paper_title: Advances and Open Problems in Federated Learning
record.original_question: How can cross-device federated-learning systems quantify and mitigate system-induced bias caused by availability profiles, device performance, network connectivity, CPU load, local dataset size, timeouts, and other factors that affect whether a device contributes to a round?

evidence.quote: study how bias can be quantified and subsequently mitigated

artifact.status_search_result: The problem remains an active research area. Several recent works partially address it: a 2023 INFOCOM paper "Tackling System Induced Bias in Federated Learning" proposes methods to quantify bias relative to time-varying client availability; a 2024 ACM FAccT paper addresses group bias due to heterogeneous devices; and recent surveys (2024–2025) catalogue mitigation techniques but explicitly list system-induced participation bias as an open challenge. No comprehensive, provably optimal framework jointly handling all listed system factors is established.

status_evidence.title: Tackling System Induced Bias in Federated Learning
status_evidence.snippet: Quantifies bias of the global model with respect to local models and time-varying client availability.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress on quantifying system-induced bias via client availability.

status_evidence.title: Mitigating Group Bias in Federated Learning for Heterogeneous Devices
status_evidence.snippet: Proposes multiplicative weight updates to mitigate bias due to feature heterogeneity across heterogeneous devices.
status_evidence.claim: Partial mitigation strategy for device-heterogeneity-induced bias.

status_evidence.title: Bias in Federated Learning: A Comprehensive Survey
status_evidence.snippet: Comprehensive survey of bias sources and mitigations in FL, listing open issues.
status_evidence.claim: Recent survey indicates many aspects of system-induced bias remain open.
